content: Regulatory surface: SEC charged Nathan Fuller / Privvy Investments (May 2026) over a $12.3M fake-AI-trading-bot scheme, ~150 investors, $6.2M misappropriated, $5.5M Ponzi-like payments. CFTC has standing customer advisories - 'AI Won't Turn Trading Bots into Money Machines' and an AI-scam advisory. Legal baseline: bots are legal in the US but every anti-fraud/anti-manipulation rule applying to a human applies to the bot and its operator. The enforcement pattern targets PERFORMANCE CLAIMS and pooled/custodied funds, not the software itself - which is exactly why 'no custody, user-owned accounts, no return promises, no leaderboard' is a compliance posture, not just modesty.
